chapter: San Francisco, the So Different Orchestra and Johnny
title: Playing classical toe-dance music at the Portola Louvre
summary: The band had to learn ballet and toe-dance music in rehearsals, preferred by management over the white orchestra despite stumbling over it.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: When we went to work in the Portola Louvre, we had never played a lot of classical dances, like for toe dances and things. We had been playing for jazz singers and jazz tapdancers and Texas Tommy [a dance], which was famous those days--and that's long before the Charleston or the Blackbottom had ever come out. It's called "Texas Tommy," and we used to play for all of that kind of stuff but when we got down there and those girls doing their toe

dancing things, commenced to bring us that classical act music and things like...uh, I can't think of it...Don's...Doll Dance and whatever... I don't remember all that--the classical music. We had to take our mornings and go off to one of our boy's homes and rehearse it, so it would...but, still, I think as bad as we played it, they wouldn't let the white orchestra play it. They preferred us to play it. The white orchestra was fiddles and piano and flute and things. They had a sweet, beautiful orchestra, and they were fine musicians but they wanted us to play it. I don't know why. And they used to let the white orchestra go at nine o'clock at night. They'd play from...we'd go in at two and play till five and do the show and then we'd go off and stay till 7:30 or eight o'clock, and when the white orchestra filling in, we'd have to come back and work the rest of the night playing for the show...two shows and the dancing and everything, and they preferred us. But I think they played the classical music better than we did. But we got along that way, and they done all the "Dance of the Flowers," I think, and "Dances of ...something" and all of those classical dances...your things...
Ballet music, yeah. That's what we used to fumble over and stumble over, but they liked it. They liked the way we played.
